content: Montgomery Regional Hospital, commonly referred to as MRH, is a healthcare facility located in the town of Blacksburg, within Montgomery County, Virginia. It operates as a subsidiary of the Hospital Corporation of America (HCA). Montgomery Regional Hospital is officially certified as a Level III trauma center, indicating its capability to provide comprehensive emergency medical services and trauma care. The hospital was established in the year 1971. On August 20, 2006, a tragic incident occurred at MRH when William Morva, who was in custody awaiting trial for an attempted robbery charge, fatally shot Derrick McFarland, a security guard stationed in the hospital's emergency department. Morva had been transported to the hospital from jail after sustaining a sprained ankle and wrist. While at the hospital, he requested to use the restroom, during which he attacked both the security guard and a Montgomery County sheriff's deputy. Following the attack, Morva managed to escape from the emergency department. He was apprehended the following day, but during his escape, he shot and killed Montgomery County Sheriff's Corporal Eric Sutphin on the morning of August 21, 2006. On April 16, 2007, during the Virginia Tech massacre, Montgomery Regional Hospital received and treated several patients who had sustained injuries in the tragic mass shooting.
